info.title: Ryu Passport API
info.summary: Encrypted, tenant-separated identity connections for agents: profiles, connections, logins, authenticated fetch and usage.
info.description: Ryu Passport stores per-domain login state for agents and never returns it. Administration routes take the tenant administration token; `/v1/runtime/*` takes a profile-scoped runtime grant, and the fetch route accepts either. Passport is in early access: Ryu provisions hosted keys, and its source is not yet published. A local process binds `http://127.0.0.1:8093` by default. A client address that keeps presenting unknown tokens gets `429` with `Retry-After`. Every error is JSON with `error` and a stable `code` (`PassportError`); a request whose Accept names `application/problem+json` gets RFC 9457 problem details. `POST /v1/connections` honours an optional `Idempotency-Key` header (see that operation). The MCP OAuth custody routes are a separate contract and are not in this document.

post.description: Creates a `NEEDS_AUTH` connection with `IDLE` flow status. A Passport whose capabilities list `features.idempotency_keys: true` honours an optional `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the tenant): a retry with the same key and body answers with the first result and `Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of creating a second connection, the same key with a different body gets `409 idempotency_conflict`, and a retry while the first still runs gets `409 idempotency_in_progress` with `Retry-After`. Without the header every request creates a connection. The `@ryuhq/services` SDK sends a key it generates, and retries the create with it after a network error, timeout or 5xx, only when `GET /v1/capabilities` lists `features.idempotency_keys: true`; otherwise it never retries this create. A key you supply is always sent.

Never retried by `@ryuhq/services` on a network error or 5xx.

AdminBearer.description: The tenant administration token (`RYU_PASSPORT_API_TOKEN` or `RYU_PASSPORT_API_TOKENS` on the service; `RYU_PASSPORT_API_KEY` for `@ryuhq/services`).

RuntimeBearer.description: A runtime grant token from `RYU_PASSPORT_RUNTIME_GRANTS` on the service (`RYU_PASSPORT_RUNTIME_KEY` for `@ryuhq/services`), bound to one tenant and a list of profiles.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Defaults to 100; values above the route's cap are clamped to it.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional on `POST /v1/connections`: a quoted Structured Field String or bare token of 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the tenant. Keys are kept for up to 24 hours (each tenant keeps at most 10,000, dropping the oldest completed first). The same key and body replays the first result with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; a different body gets `409 idempotency_conflict`, and a request while the first still runs gets `409 idempotency_in_progress` with `Retry-After`.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Optional on `POST /v1/connections`: a quoted Structured Field String or bare token of 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, scoped to the tenant. Keys are kept for up to 24 hours (each tenant keeps at most 10,000, dropping the oldest completed first). The same key and body replays the first result with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; a different body gets `409 idempotency_conflict`, and a request while the first still runs gets `409 idempotency_in_progress` with `Retry-After`.

UsageFrom.name: from
UsageFrom.description: Window start, included: an RFC 3339 UTC time on a whole hour.

UsageTo.name: to
UsageTo.description: Window end, excluded: an RFC 3339 UTC time on a whole hour, after `from` and at most 31 days later.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota for the policy in effect, per draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11 (a Structured Field List, e.g. `"default";r=0;t=30`). Sent by the limiters that expose a remaining count; the per-key API limiter does not yet, so a 429 here may carry no rate-limit fields.

RateLimitPolicy.description: The quota policy, per draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11 (a Structured Field List, e.g. `"default";q=100;w=60`).

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (RFC 9110 §10.2.3), when the server knows it.

Deprecation.description: Present only on a deprecated route: when it was or will be deprecated, as an RFC 9745 Structured Field Date (`@<unix seconds>`). No route is deprecated today.

Sunset.description: Present only on a deprecated route with a removal date: the HTTP-date after which it may stop responding (RFC 8594).

Link.description: On a deprecated route, `rel="deprecation"` links the versioning and deprecation policy (RFC 9745 §3) and `rel="successor-version"` the replacement.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when the response is a replay stored for the request's `Idempotency-Key`.

WWWAuthenticate.description: Bearer challenge (RFC 6750) naming the protected resource metadata (RFC 9728 `resource_metadata`).

auth_required.description: Whether `/v1` routes need a tenant bearer; always true.

features.description: Whether each feature is on, by name, such as `idempotency_keys` or `problem_details`.

Connection.description: One per-domain login. Sealed credential state is structurally absent from every response.

profile_id.description: Your own id for whose credentials these are.

domain.description: The host the connection may fetch.

status.description: Durable state: `AUTHENTICATED` holds sealed credential state; `NEEDS_AUTH` needs a login.

source.description: The credential source that captured it; `manual` by default.

last_checked.description: Unix seconds of the last health check; 0 when never checked.

profiles.description: Every profile that has a connection.

status.description: Durable state: `AUTHENTICATED` holds sealed credential state; `NEEDS_AUTH` needs a login.

profile_id.description: Your own id for whose credentials these are, such as `work`.

domain.description: The host the connection may fetch, such as `api.github.com`.

source.description: A credential source id; when omitted the operator's registry picks one by domain.

kind.description: `hosted`: open `url` to log in. `manual`: capture the credential state yourself and import it.

url.description: The page to open to log in.

state.description: Captured credential state; sealed before it is stored.

HeaderPart.description: One part of a structured credential header: literal text, caller-supplied sensitive text (redacted from the answer), or `vault:<domain>` state.

sensitive.description: Caller-supplied text sent as it is but redacted from the answer.

vault.description: A domain whose stored connection state is inserted here; it must be the request's domain.

url.description: HTTPS on the connection's exact domain and port 443.

body.description: A JSON body, for methods the credential is granted.

headers.description: Plain request headers, sent as they are.

headerTemplates.description: Headers built from parts (literal, sensitive or `vault:<domain>` state), by header name.

maxContentChars.description: Truncate the answer's `content` to this many characters.

authenticated.description: Whether a credential was attached, not whether the provider accepted it.

content.description: The upstream body as text, with credential values redacted.

meters.description: `connectionSeconds`: seconds each connection existed inside the window, summed. `fetches`: authenticated fetches and MCP transport calls in the window that got a response from their upstream.

connectionSeconds.description: Seconds each connection existed inside the window, summed.

fetches.description: Authenticated fetches and MCP transport calls in the window that got a response from their upstream.

PassportError.description: Every Passport error: the JSON body, or its RFC 9457 form when the request's Accept names `application/problem+json`. Branch on `code`, not on `error` text. Unknown routes answer `404 not_found` and a wrong method `405 method_not_allowed` with `Allow`.

PassportErrorBody.description: `error` is the message Passport has always sent; `code` is stable. `ok: false` and `message` are added on usage-window `invalid_request`, `insufficient_credits` and `metering_unavailable`, where `error` repeats the code.

error.description: The error message, or the code where `message` is sent.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person.

PassportProblem.description: RFC 9457 problem details, sent only when the request's Accept names `application/problem+json`: the standard members plus every `PassportErrorBody` member, in no particular order.

type.description: The problem type: `https://docs.ryuhq.com/docs/standalone/passport-api#<code>`, an anchor in the API page's error-code table.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person.

PassportErrorCode.description: Stable error codes. Branch on these, not on messages.
